sections.text_helper: Section 64.9.13 "I3C IBI transfer, as controller/target" in chapter 64 (Improved inter-integrated circuit (I3C)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 3208.
sections.section_content:
Figure830 illustrates IBI (in-band interrupt) transfer, as communicated on the I3C bus, and
as programmed when acting as target or received as controller.
[Figure 830. IBI transfer, as controller/target]
When the I3C peripheral acts as controller, the I3C_IBIDR register is used to receive the IBI
data payload. Consequently, the IBI request from the target must not exceed a 4-byte data
payload. If there is more information to be exchanged in the context of this in-band interrupt,
the controller software must issue a private read.
Timing control and sensor acquisition timestamping when I3C controller
When the I3C peripheral acts a controller, it can use timing control and asynchronous mode0
to timestamp the moment at which the target(s) acquired sampled data, and to time-
correlate them.
To do this, the software must go through the following sequence:
1. Allocate and configure a timer in capture mode, to be connected to the I3C generated
event i3c_ibi_ack so that for each IBI acknowledge the counter of the timer can be
captured.
2. Program a broadcast/direct SETXTIME CCC with sub-command byte 0xDT to enter
asynchronous mode 0 on the target(s) side.
3. After being notified of the command completion by the flag and/or the related interrupt
(FCF flag is set in I3C_EVR register), reset and enable the timer to start the counter on
the controller side.
4. After being notified that an IBI is complete by the flag and/or the related interrupt
(IBIF=1 in the I3C_EVR register), and if the IBI is with timing info (if IBIDB0[7:5] = 100
in the I3C_IBIDR register), read the captured value of the timer, as C_TIM. Given that:
a) C_C2 = 9 × (SCLL_PP[7:0] + 1 + SCLH_I3C[7:0] + 1) × TI3CCLK
b) T_C1 (16-bit value) = {IBIDB2, IBIDB1} in the I3C_IBIDR register
c) T_C2 (8-bit value) = IBID3 in the I3C_IBIDR register
Compute the timestamp of the sampled data received from the target, as follows (see
MIPI spec formula for more details): C_TS = C_TIM - C_C2 x T_C1 / T_C2.
5. Repeat step 4, for each received IBI.
6. Generate a broadcast/direct SETXTIME CCC with subcommand byte 0xFF to exit
asynchronous mode 0 and disable/deallocate the timer resource.
